chapter: Career overview and the Lunceford quarrel
title: Broadway musicals, records and buying the Bronx house
summary: Crawford describes playing over 21 Broadway musicals starting with a Billy Kyle show, making records, and paying off his large house in two years.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: And I was living at 513 Edgecombe. That's there at 159 150th and 9th and Edgecombe with that little lady there. So I finally started to playing those Broadway musicals and making records with everybody, records on top of records, Jackie Gleason, Ethel Merman, Carol Channing, Carol Bruce.
Well, I tell you what. You go ahead, and when you get to the end, then we'll go back.
Then I finally saved up enough money, Stanley, and bought this mausoleum here.
Twelve or 14 rooms around in here somewhere. Bought it, and

I paid for it in two years. I didn't want to pay no notes and interest and all that. We paid it off in two years. And so here I am (Inaudible) right now, very happy; at least I accomplished something out of all I did in the music business, started out with nothing, wound up with this, car in the garage, which is snowbound. So I did something, and I'm very proud of old Jimmy Crawford.
I'm very arrogant and egotistical and I don't know what all you call me. But when I'm with you, I'm going to stay with you, be with you all the way through. [Stick it out until] the end.

Oh, yeah, the pianist, Billy Kyle. He was rehearsing a show downtown by the name of "Alive and Kicking," I think, and they wanted a drummer, colored drummer supposed to be a swing drummer, because when you're in the pits, you have no reason to be flashy, like in a Broadway musical.
So I went in that show, and I played over 21 Broadway musicals. They really set me up. You know, I told you about that.
